title: Sapta Swara Metaphysics, Devatas, Rishis & Iconographic Attributes Database
description: Authoritative musicological dataset detailing the metaphysical, spiritual, aesthetic, iconographic, and physical attributes of the Sapta Swaras (S, R, G, M, P, D, N) and Shodasa Swarasthanas, tagged with scholarly treatise citations.

scholarly_treatise_bibliography.author: N. S. Ramachandran
scholarly_treatise_bibliography.relevance: Details historical evolution of Swaras, Srutis, Vedic chants, and ancient treatise references (pp. 12-25).

scholarly_treatise_bibliography.author: Sārangadeva (c. 1230 AD)
scholarly_treatise_bibliography.relevance: Svarādhyāya (Chapter 1, Section 3, Verses 46-59): Primary authority for Swara Devatas, Rishis, Varnas, Chhandas, Rasas, and Animal sound analogies.

scholarly_treatise_bibliography.author: Bharata Muni (c. 200 BC - 200 AD)
scholarly_treatise_bibliography.relevance: Chapters 28 & 29: Earliest extant classification of Swara-Rasa associations, Grama systems, and Sruti allocations.

scholarly_treatise_bibliography.author: Sage Narada (c. 1st Century AD)
scholarly_treatise_bibliography.relevance: First text to establish explicit correspondence between Samavedic chant accents, lay notes, animal sounds, and Devatas (1.5.1-7).

scholarly_treatise_bibliography.author: Matanga Muni (c. 800 AD)
scholarly_treatise_bibliography.relevance: Defines the acoustic origin of Swara from Sruti and connects Swaras with physical body registers and spiritual deities (verses 61-78).

scholarly_treatise_bibliography.author: Narada (c. 11th Century AD)
scholarly_treatise_bibliography.relevance: Elaborates on the iconographic colors, castes (Varnas), and planetary ruler ships of the Sapta Swaras.

scholarly_treatise_bibliography.author: National Institute of Open Schooling / Traditional Curriculum
scholarly_treatise_bibliography.relevance: Foundational textbook outlining Dwadasa/Shodasa Swarasthana definitions, origin of Indian music, and introductory theory.

sapta_swara_metaphysics.meaning_and_etymology: Born of six organs: throat, chest, palate, nose, tongue, and teeth (Sat + Ja). The fundamental tonic anchor of all music.

animal_bird_analogy.sound_description: The joyous crying of the peacock at the onset of rain-bearing monsoon clouds.

presiding_deity.iconographic_significance: Agni represents the primordial spark of breath (Prana) ignited at the Muladhara chakra.

sapta_swara_metaphysics.color_varna: Padmapatra (Lotus Leaf Pink / Radiant White / Rose)
sapta_swara_metaphysics.body_resonance_register: Nose, throat, chest, palate, tongue, teeth (6-organ resonance starting at Muladhara)

sapta_swara_metaphysics.meaning_and_etymology: Derived from Rishabha (the powerful Bull), symbolizing strength, vigor, and upward ascent.

animal_bird_analogy.sound_description: The deep, resonant bellowing of a bull calling its herd or a mother cow calling her calf.

presiding_deity.iconographic_significance: Represents the creative impulse expanding through speech and vocal resonance.

sapta_swara_metaphysics.color_varna: Pīta / Gauravarṇa (Pale Yellow / Tawny / Golden Amber)

sapta_swara_metaphysics.meaning_and_etymology: Associated with the fragrance (Gandha) of music and the ancient Gandhara region.

animal_bird_analogy.sound_description: The bleating of a goat or ram in the mountain pastures.

presiding_deity.iconographic_significance: Embodies subtle intellectual sweetness, artistic refinement, and meditative absorption.

sapta_swara_metaphysics.meaning_and_etymology: The central or middle note of the Sapta Swara octave, dividing Purvanga and Uttaranga.

animal_bird_analogy.sound_description: The cry of the Krauncha crane echoing across peaceful waters.

presiding_deity.iconographic_significance: Sustaining pivot of musical harmony; indestructible intermediate pillar.

sapta_swara_metaphysics.color_varna: Kundapuṣpa / Śukla (Pure Jasmine White / Pearl White)

sapta_swara_metaphysics.meaning_and_etymology: The fifth note of the scale; fixed invariant consonant (Samvadi) to Sadja.

animal_bird_analogy.sound_description: The sweet fifth-tone call of the Kokila bird in spring gardens.

presiding_deity.primary_devata: Nāradī / Lord Viṣṇu / Sun God / Goddess Caṇḍī
presiding_deity.iconographic_significance: Panchama is the immutable pillar of stability and cosmic sweet resonance.

sapta_swara_metaphysics.color_varna: Kṛṣṇa / Nīla / Syama (Dark Blue / Deep Indigo / Crimson Black)
sapta_swara_metaphysics.body_resonance_register: 5 Body Resonant Places (Navel, Chest, Heart, Throat, Head)

sapta_swara_metaphysics.meaning_and_etymology: Imbued with Dhi (intellectual stability and reposed wisdom).

animal_bird_analogy.sound_description: The triumphant neighing of a noble horse or the deep call of an elephant.

presiding_deity.iconographic_significance: Represents intellect, strength, and steady foundation before the octave culmination.

sapta_swara_metaphysics.color_varna: Pīta / Gaura (Golden Yellow / Amber / Bright Ochre)

sapta_swara_metaphysics.meaning_and_etymology: The note in which all previous swaras settle or rest (Nisidanti asmin svarah).

animal_bird_analogy.sound_description: The majestic trumpeting of a regal elephant at dawn.

presiding_deity.iconographic_significance: Culmination of the scale leading seamlessly into Tara Sadja.
